items.stem: What approach does IAS 12 use to measure deferred tax?

options.text: The temporary-difference (balance-sheet) approach based on differences between carrying amounts and tax bases
options.rationale: Correct: deferred tax is based on temporary differences between carrying amount and tax base.

options.text: A timing-difference approach based only on the income statement
options.rationale: IAS 12 uses the balance-sheet temporary-difference approach.

options.text: Discounting all future tax payments to present value
A flat percentage of accounting profit
options.rationale: Deferred tax is not a flat percentage of profit.

items.explanation: Correct: deferred tax is based on temporary differences between carrying amount and tax base.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO conditions are relevant to recognising a deferred tax asset for unused tax losses? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is probable that future taxable profit will be available against which the losses can be used
options.rationale: Correct: recoverability against future taxable profits is required.

options.text: The losses relate to temporary differences or carry-forwards that are deductible in the future
options.rationale: Correct: the asset must represent a future deductible benefit.

options.text: The entity has paid a dividend in the period
options.rationale: Dividend payment is irrelevant to recognising a deferred tax asset.

options.text: The directors wish to improve reported profit
options.rationale: Management preference is not a recognition condition.

items.explanation: Correct: recoverability against future taxable profits is required.

items.stem: A company measures its deferred tax liability by discounting the expected future tax payments to present value. Why is this inappropriate under IAS 12?

options.text: IAS 12 prohibits discounting deferred tax assets and liabilities
options.rationale: Correct: deferred tax balances are not discounted.

options.text: Deferred tax must always be discounted at the risk-free rate
options.rationale: The opposite is true: discounting is prohibited.

options.text: Deferred tax liabilities are never recognised
options.rationale: Deferred tax liabilities are recognised; they are just not discounted.

options.text: Discounting is only allowed for current tax
options.rationale: Neither current nor deferred tax is discounted in this way.

items.explanation: Correct: deferred tax balances are not discounted.
